headline: Oncology models import external references and other modalities to improve prediction
label: Cross Modal Cancer Prediction
summary: New preprints link bulk, single-cell, cfDNA and histology data through external references, as in mFrag, DeSCENT, OmniT2I and KLONE.
synthesis: The dominant thread is injecting information from external references or complementary modalities into data-limited cancer prediction. mFrag weights cfDNA fragmentomic features with external methylation atlases for early lung cancer detection. DeSCENT derives reference-informed cellular profiles from bulk RNA-seq for TCGA survival models. SigBridgeR standardizes eight algorithms that map bulk phenotypes onto single-cell subpopulations. KLONE assigns unpaired scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq copy-number clones with an imbalance-robust k-NN ensemble. OmniT2I renders molecular profiles as images, fuses them with histopathology embeddings, and infers missing modalities. Survival work splits between adding signal and constraining it. EvoSurv adds a 38-dimensional evolutionary representation to clinical and RNA data. CAISL anchors LUAD models on clinical variables with sparse molecular correction. A 1.3M-slide study maps how much sex, age and race H&E foundation-model features encode, which bears on confounding in transferred representations. Peripheral items cover cell typing, hierarchical subtyping, compositional benchmarking and scDNA cell calling.
